entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Christian Charles Josias, Baron von Bunsen, was a German diplomat and scholar born in 1795 in Schönebeck, Saxony-Anhalt, to a noble family. He worked in the Papal States and England for a large part of his career, serving as a diplomat and ambassador to various European powers. Von Bunsen was a key figure in the development of the modern diplomatic corps and played a significant role in shaping European politics during the 19th century. He was a strong advocate for the principles of international law and cooperation, and his work had a lasting impact on the development of modern diplomacy.


Von Bunsen was also a prolific scholar and writer, publishing numerous works on history, politics, and philosophy. He was a close friend and correspondent of prominent figures such as Lord Byron and Prince Metternich, and his correspondence provides valuable insights into the politics and culture of the time.


Despite his many accomplishments, von Bunsen's life was not without controversy. He was involved in several high-profile diplomatic incidents, including the Affair of the Pope, which led to his temporary expulsion from the Papal States. However, his reputation and influence endured, and he remained a respected figure in European politics until his death in 1860.


In the years following his death, von Bunsen's work experienced a resurgence in popularity, and he is now recognized as one of the most important diplomats and scholars of the 19th century. His legacy continues to be felt in the modern diplomatic corps, and his contributions to the development of international law and cooperation remain an essential part of our understanding of the modern world.


As a testament to his enduring influence, von Bunsen's letters and diplomatic correspondence are now held in high esteem by historians and scholars, providing a unique window into the politics and culture of 19th-century Europe.
